# From programs to circuits {#digital-design .section-title .center}

## Digital design, briefly {#digital-design-seed}

- RTL and hardware description languages
- Combinational versus sequential behavior
- Synthesis, placement, and the multi-stage design flow

# MLIR for hardware {#circt .section-title .center}

## Why CIRCT? {#circt-seed}

- Hardware concepts represented as dialects
- Modules, values, combinational logic, state, and control
- Progressive lowering from intent to RTL

# CIRCT in practice {#circt-tools .section-title .center}

## Toolchain checkpoint {#circt-tools-seed}

- Import and inspect a small design
- Run transformations and synthesis
- Compare structure, metrics, and equivalence

# Arithmetic becomes hardware {#arithmetic .section-title .center}

## One E4M3 multiplier {#arithmetic-seed}

- Match floating-point arithmetic in MLIR
- Build the equivalent CIRCT `comb` network
- Decode, multiply, normalize, round, and pack

# HLS with MLIR and CIRCT {#hls .section-title .center}

## Scheduling and pipelines {#hls-seed}

- Move from one operator to a scheduled datapath
- Make latency, resources, and control explicit
- Connect the exercise to the EuroLLVM HLS material
